To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified FBXO7, a gene involved in protein degradation, as the cause of Parkinsonian-pyamidal syndrome, a disorder characterized by parkinsonism and pyramidal signs, and that a 500 K genome-wide SNP array is a valuable tool for linkage studies.

1) we performed a linkage analysis on a large family affected with Parkinsonian-Pyramidal Syndrome using 500 K SNP chip arrays; 2) we identified linkage to a region on chromosome 22 and sequenced candidate genes; 3) we identified a disease-associated variation (R378 G) in FBX07, a gene involved in ubiquitin-proteasome protein degradation; 4) we assessed the performance of 500 K SNP chips in linkage studies and demonstrated that

(i) the use of high-density SNP arrays is an effective tool for genome-wide linkage analysis; (ii) the use of 10 K chip platforms for linkage analysis is likely to be less effective, and (iii) FBXO7 is a gene that may be involved in the pathogenesis of Parkinsonian-pyridal syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of 500 K SNP array for genome-wide linkage analysis.
the development of high-throughput genotyping technology and the application of the technology to the identification of a novel gene.
the use of high-density SNP arrays for linkage studies, and the results show the value of using 500 K SNP chips.

the use of 500 K arrays is a viable option for genome-wide linkage studies, especially when the disease-causing gene has a low allele frequency.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of 500 K arrays for genome-wide linkage studies is feasible and can be cost-effective, particularly when the disease locus is expected to have a high allele frequency.
the 500 K array is a valuable tool for genome-wide linkage studies and can be used to detect linkage to a disease in a large pedigree with high confidence.
, in order to detect linkage in a complex disease, it may be necessary to use a SNP array that interrogates at least 100,000 polymorphisms across the genome.
